name: Weights copy through W
summary: A weight diag(1, r) on the input of a W-node can be pushed onto each of its outputs.
description:
The W-node (black triangle) with one input and $n$ outputs maps $|0\rangle \mapsto |0\cdots 0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle \mapsto |10\cdots0\rangle + |010\cdots0\rangle + \cdots + |0\cdots01\rangle$: it spreads a single excitation over its outputs in all possible ways. The small dot marks its input leg.

In the $R$-labelled ZW-calculus $\mathrm{ZW}_R$, the white vertex with label $r$ (here a Z-box) with two legs is the map $\mathrm{diag}(1, r) = |0\rangle\langle 0| + r|1\rangle\langle 1|$. Because each term produced by the W-node has at most one excitation, a weight $r$ on the input is the same as a weight $r$ on each output: every label is a comonoid homomorphism for the W-node.

With $r = e^{i\alpha}$ this pushes Z-phases through a W-node, and with $r = -1$ it is [Z(π) commutes through W](../w-pi-commutation/).
parameter_notes: m is the number of outputs of the W-node (shown for m = 2); holds for any m.

source.location: Chapter 5, Section 5.2 (list of rules of the ZW calculus), rule $nat_c^r$
